title: बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा पशुका अवशेष खोजी र व्यवस्थापन धमाधम
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । गत भदौ १० गते भोटेकोशी आएको बाढीले क्षति पुर्‍याएको क्षेत्रमा स्थानीयले पशुका अवशेष खोज्ने तथा व्यवस्थापन गर्ने काम जारी राखेका छन् । बाढीले बंगुर, बाख्रा तथा कुखुरापालन फार्ममा क्षति पुर्‍याएपछि हराएका पशुका अवशेष खोज्न स्थानीय सक्रिय भएका हुन् । स्थानीय फूलबहादुर तामाङले भदौ १० गते आएको बाढीले क्षति पुर्‍याएको क्षेत्रमा पशुका अवशेष खोज्ने तथा व्यवस्थापन गर्ने काम भइरहेको बताए । उनले वडाबाट ३० जनाको समिति गठन गरी बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा खोजी तथा सरसफाइको काम भइरहेको बताए । उनले बाढीले क्षति पु¥याएका बंगुर तथा बाख्रा फार्महरूमा पुगेर पशुका हड्डी तथा अवशेष खोज्ने र भेटिएका अवशेषलाई खाल्डो खनेर गाड्ने काम भइरहेको जानकारी दिए । हालसम्म दुई ठाउँमा पशुका हड्डी भेटिएको र ती सबै व्यवस्थापन गरिसकिएको उनको भनाइ छ । उनले बाढीका कारण जंगल आसपास तथा माथिल्लो गाउँका स्थानीयले सञ्चालन गरेका बाख्रा र बंगुर फार्ममा ठूलो क्षति पुगेको बताए । स्थानीयले जीविकोपार्जनका लागि आठ–दश वटासम्म बाख्रा र दुई–चार वटासम्म बंगुर पाल्दै आएका थिए। तर बाढीले फार्म तथा पशुपालन व्यवसायमा क्षति हुँदा उनीहरूको आम्दानीको स्रोत नै गुमेको उनले बताए । तामाङका अनुसार बाढीपछि स्थानीय कृषकले सडक र खानेपानीको समस्या भोगिरहेका छन् । बाढीले बाटो भत्काउनुका साथै खानेपानीका मुहान तथा सिँचाइका संरचना पुरिएका कारण पानीको अभावसमेत भएको छ । बाढी आउनुअघि स्थानीयले खेतबारीमा तरकारीलगायत खेती गर्दै जीविकोपार्जन गरिरहेका थिए । तर बाढीले खेतीयोग्य जमिन र उत्पादन बगाएपछि अहिले तत्काल आम्दानी गर्ने माध्यम नरहेको उनले बताए । स्थानीय सरकारले सडक तथा आवतजावत सहज बनाउने कामलाई प्राथमिकता दिए पनि प्रभावित परिवारका लागि तत्काल आयआर्जनको वातावरण बनाउन आवश्यक रहेको उनको भनाइ छ । उनले भने, ‘माथिल्लो गाउँमा बसिरहेका मानिसहरूका लागि फेरि कमाएर खाने वातावरण बनाउन सकियो भने राम्रो हुन्थ्यो। हामीले काम सुरु गरेको १०–१५ दिन भइसक्यो। अझै १०–१५ दिनसम्म खोजी तथा व्यवस्थापनको काम गर्नुपर्ने अवस्था छ ।’ उनका अनुसार बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा पशुका अवशेष खोज्ने र व्यवस्थापन गर्ने काम अझै जारी छ । यसैगरी, कृषबहादुर तामाङले भदौ १० गतेको बाढीले क्षति पु¥याएका क्षेत्रमा पशुका अवशेष खोज्ने काम जारी रहेको बताए । उनका अनुसार बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रका अधिकांश स्थानमा खोजी तथा छानबिन गरिएको छ । केही ठाउँमा पशुका हड्डी तथा अवशेष भेटिए पनि कतिपय स्थानमा भने अहिलेसम्म केही फेला परेको छैन । भेटिएका स्थानमा अवशेष पहिचान गर्ने र व्यवस्थापन गर्ने प्रयास भइरहेको उनले बताए । तामाङका अनुसार बाढी आउनुअघि उक्त क्षेत्रमा बंगुर तथा कुखुरापालनका फार्महरू सञ्चालनमा थिए । जलविद्युत् आयोजनामा काम गर्ने टोलीसमेत बस्ने गरेको उक्त क्षेत्रमा पसल तथा पशुपालन फार्महरू रहेका थिए । उनले आफ्नो अनुमानमा उक्त क्षेत्रमा दुईदेखि चार वटासम्म बंगुर तथा कुखुराका फार्म रहेको बताए। बाढीले ती फार्महरूमा ठूलो क्षति पु¥याएपछि अहिले हराएका पशुका अवशेष खोज्ने काम भइरहेको उनको भनाइ छ । खोजीका क्रममा कुनै स्थानमा हड्डी भेटिएको र कुनै स्थानमा नभेटिएको भन्दै उनले सम्पूर्ण क्षेत्रको खोजी पूरा नभएसम्म प्रयास जारी राख्ने बताए। हड्डीबाहेक अन्य सामग्री वा अवशेष भने अहिलेसम्म फेला नपरेको उनले जानकारी दिए । Kathmandu. Locals are continuing to search for and manage the remains of animals in the area damaged by the Bhotekoshi flood on Bhadra 10. Locals have become active in searching for the remains of missing animals after the flood damaged pig, goat and poultry farms. Local Phul Bahadur Tamang said that work is underway to search for and manage animal remains in the area damaged by the flood that occurred on Bhadra 20. He said that a committee of 30 people from the ward has been formed to search and clean up the flood-affected area. He informed that work is underway to search for animal bones and remains in flood-damaged pig and goat farms and dig pits to bury the remains found. He said that so far, animal bones have been found in two places and all of them have been managed. He said that the floods have caused major damage to goat and pig farms run by locals in the forest and upper villages. The locals used to raise eight to ten goats and two to four pigs for their livelihood. But the floods have damaged their farms and livestock farming businesses, and they have lost their source of income, he said. According to Tamang, local farmers are facing problems with roads and drinking water after the floods. The floods have destroyed roads and buried drinking water sources and irrigation structures, leading to water shortages. Before the flood, locals were earning a living by cultivating vegetables and other crops in their fields. But now, after the flood washed away the cultivable land and produce, there is no immediate way to earn an income, he said. He said that although the local government has prioritized the work of improving roads and facilitating movement, it is necessary to create an immediate income-generating environment for the affected families. He said, "It would be good if we could create an environment where people living in the upper villages can earn a living again. It has been 10-15 days since we started the work. There is still 10-15 days of search and management work to be done." According to him, the work of searching for and managing animal remains in the flood-affected areas is still ongoing. Similarly, Krish Bahadur Tamang said that work is ongoing to search for animal remains in areas damaged by the floods of Bhadra 20. According to him, searches and investigations have been carried out in most of the flood-affected areas. While animal bones and remains have been found in some places, nothing has been found in others. He said that efforts are being made to identify and manage the remains in the places where they are found. According to Tamang, before the flood, pig and poultry farms were operating in the area. There were shops and livestock farms in the area, where the team working on the hydroelectric project also lived. He estimated that there were two to four pig and chicken farms in the area. He said that efforts are underway to find the remains of the missing animals after the floods caused extensive damage to those farms. Stating that bones were found in some places during the search and not in others, he said that efforts will continue until the search of the entire area is completed. He informed that other materials or remains other than bones have not been found so far.

गर्ने काम भइरहेको बताए । उनले वडाबाट ३० जनाको समिति गठन गरी बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा खोजी तथा सरसफाइको काम भइरहेको बताए । उनले बाढीले क्षति पु¥याएका बंगुर तथा बाख्रा फार्महरूमा पुगेर पशुका हड्डी तथा अवशेष खोज्ने र भेटिएका अवशेषलाई खाल्डो खनेर गाड्ने काम भइरहेको जानकारी दिए । हालसम्म दुई ठाउँमा पशुका हड्डी भेटिएको र ती सबै व्यवस्थापन गरिसकिएको उनको भनाइ छ । उनले बाढीका कारण जंगल आसपास तथा माथिल्लो गाउँका स्थानीयले सञ्चालन गरेका बाख्रा र बंगुर फार्ममा ठूलो क्षति पुगेको बताए । स्थानीयले जीविकोपार्जनका लागि आठ–दश वटासम्म बाख्रा र दुई–चार वटासम्म बंगुर पाल्दै आएका थिए। तर बाढीले फार्म तथा पशुपालन व्यवसायमा क्षति हुँदा उनीहरूको आम्दानीको स्रोत नै गुमेको उनले बताए । तामाङका अनुसार बाढीपछि स्थानीय कृषकले सडक र खानेपानीको समस्या भोगिरहेका छन् । बाढीले बाटो भत्काउनुका साथै खानेपानीका मुहान तथा सिँचाइका संरचना पुरिएका कारण पानीको अभावसमेत भएको छ । बाढी आउनुअघि स्थानीयले खेतबारीमा तरकारीलगायत खेती गर्दै जीविकोपार्जन गरिरहेका थिए । तर बाढीले खेतीयोग्य जमिन र उत्पादन बगाएपछि अहिले तत्काल आम्दानी गर्ने माध्यम नरहेको उनले बताए । स्थानीय सरकारले सडक तथा आवतजावत सहज बनाउने कामलाई प्राथमिकता दिए पनि प्रभावित परिवारका लागि तत्काल आयआर्जनको वातावरण बनाउन आवश्यक रहेको उनको भनाइ छ । उनले भने, ‘माथिल्लो गाउँमा बसिरहेका मानिसहरूका लागि फेरि कमाएर खाने वातावरण बनाउन सकियो भने राम्रो हुन्थ्यो। हामीले काम सुरु गरेको १०–१५ दिन भइसक्यो। अझै १०–१५ दिनसम्म खोजी तथा व्यवस्थापनको काम गर्नुपर्ने अवस्था छ ।’ उनका अनुसार बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा पशुका अवशेष खोज्ने र व्यवस्थापन गर्ने काम अझै जारी छ । यसैगरी, कृषबहादुर तामाङले भदौ १० गतेको बाढीले क्षति पु¥याएका क्षेत्रमा पशुका अवशेष खोज्ने काम जारी रहेको बताए । उनका अनुसार बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रका अधिकांश स्थानमा खोजी तथा छानबिन गरिएको छ । केही ठाउँमा पशुका हड्डी तथा अवशेष भेटिए पनि कतिपय स्थानमा भने अहिलेसम्म केही फेला परेको छैन । भेटिएका स्थानमा अवशेष पहिचान गर्ने र व्यवस्थापन गर्ने प्रयास भइरहेको उनले बताए । तामाङका अनुसार बाढी आउनुअघि उक्त क्षेत्रमा बंगुर तथा कुखुरापालनका फार्महरू सञ्चालनमा थिए । जलविद्युत् आयोजनामा काम गर्ने टोलीसमेत बस्ने गरेको उक्त क्षेत्रमा पसल तथा पशुपालन फार्महरू रहेका थिए । उनले आफ्नो अनुमानमा उक्त क्षेत्रमा दुईदेखि चार वटासम्म बंगुर तथा कुखुराका फार्म रहेको बताए। बाढीले ती फार्महरूमा ठूलो क्षति पु¥याएपछि अहिले हराएका पशुका अवशेष खोज्ने काम भइरहेको उनको भनाइ छ । खोजीका क्रममा कुनै स्थानमा हड्डी भेटिएको र कुनै स्थानमा नभेटिएको भन्दै उनले सम्पूर्ण क्षेत्रको खोजी पूरा नभएसम्म प्रयास जारी राख्ने बताए। हड्डीबाहेक अन्य सामग्री वा अवशेष भने अहिलेसम्म फेला नपरेको उनले जानकारी दिए । Kathmandu. Locals are continuing to search for and manage the remains of animals in the area damaged by the Bhotekoshi flood on Bhadra 10. Locals have become active in searching for the remains of missing animals after the flood damaged pig, goat and poultry farms. Local Phul Bahadur Tamang said that work is underway to search for and manage animal remains in the area damaged by the flood that occurred on Bhadra 20. He said that a committee of 30 people from the ward has been formed to search and clean up the flood-affected area. He informed that work is underway to search for animal bones and remains in flood-damaged pig and goat farms and dig pits to bury the remains found. He said that so far, animal bones have been found in two places and all of them have been managed. He said that the floods have caused major damage to goat and pig farms run by locals in the forest and upper villages. The locals used to raise eight to ten goats and two to four pigs for their livelihood. But the floods have damaged their farms and livestock farming businesses, and they have lost their source of income, he said. According to Tamang, local farmers are facing problems with roads and drinking water after the floods. The floods have destroyed roads and buried drinking water sources and irrigation structures, leading to water shortages. Before the flood, locals were earning a living by cultivating vegetables and other crops in their fields. But now, after the flood washed away the cultivable land and produce, there is no immediate way to earn an income, he said. He said that although the local government has prioritized the work of improving roads and facilitating movement, it is necessary to create an immediate income-generating environment for the affected families. He said, "It would be good if we could create an environment where people living in the upper villages can earn a living again. It has been 10-15 days since we started the work. There is still 10-15 days of search and management work to be done." According to him, the work of searching for and managing animal remains in the flood-affected areas is still ongoing. Similarly, Krish Bahadur Tamang said that work is ongoing to search for animal remains in areas damaged by the floods of Bhadra 20. According to him, searches and investigations have been carried out in most of the flood-affected areas. While animal bones and remains have been found in some places, nothing has been found in others. He said that efforts are being made to identify and manage the remains in the places where they are found. According to Tamang, before the flood, pig and poultry farms were operating in the area. There were shops and livestock farms in the area, where the team working on the hydroelectric project also lived. He estimated that there were two to four pig and chicken farms in the area. He said that efforts are underway to find the remains of the missing animals after the floods caused extensive damage to those farms. Stating that bones were found in some places during the search and not in others, he said that efforts will continue until the search of the entire area is completed. He informed that other materials or remains other than bones have not been found so far.

‘माथिल्लो गाउँमा बसिरहेका मानिसहरूका लागि फेरि कमाएर खाने वातावरण बनाउन सकियो भने राम्रो हुन्थ्यो। हामीले काम सुरु गरेको १०–१५ दिन भइसक्यो। अझै १०–१५ दिनसम्म खोजी तथा व्यवस्थापनको काम गर्नुपर्ने अवस्था छ ।’ उनका अनुसार बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा पशुका अवशेष खोज्ने र व्यवस्थापन गर्ने काम अझै जारी छ । यसैगरी, कृषबहादुर तामाङले भदौ १० गतेको बाढीले क्षति पु¥याएका क्षेत्रमा पशुका अवशेष खोज्ने काम जारी रहेको बताए । उनका अनुसार बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रका अधिकांश स्थानमा खोजी तथा छानबिन गरिएको छ । केही ठाउँमा पशुका हड्डी तथा अवशेष भेटिए पनि कतिपय स्थानमा भने अहिलेसम्म केही फेला परेको छैन । भेटिएका स्थानमा अवशेष पहिचान गर्ने र व्यवस्थापन गर्ने प्रयास भइरहेको उनले बताए । तामाङका अनुसार बाढी आउनुअघि उक्त क्षेत्रमा बंगुर तथा कुखुरापालनका फार्महरू सञ्चालनमा थिए । जलविद्युत् आयोजनामा काम गर्ने टोलीसमेत बस्ने गरेको उक्त क्षेत्रमा पसल तथा पशुपालन फार्महरू रहेका थिए । उनले आफ्नो अनुमानमा उक्त क्षेत्रमा दुईदेखि चार वटासम्म बंगुर तथा कुखुराका फार्म रहेको बताए। बाढीले ती फार्महरूमा ठूलो क्षति बताए। हड्डीबाहेक अन्य सामग्री वा अवशेष भने अहिलेसम्म फेला नपरेको उनले जानकारी दिए । Kathmandu. Locals are continuing to search for and manage the remains of animals in the area damaged by the Bhotekoshi flood on Bhadra 10. Locals have become active in searching for the remains of missing animals after the flood damaged pig, goat and poultry farms. Local Phul Bahadur Tamang said that work is underway to search for and manage animal remains in the area damaged by the flood that occurred on Bhadra 20. He said that a committee of 30 people from the ward has been formed to search and clean up the flood-affected area. He informed that work is underway to search for animal bones and remains in flood-damaged pig and goat farms and dig pits to bury the remains found. He said that so far, animal bones have been found in two places and all of them have been managed. He said that the floods have caused major damage to goat and pig farms run by locals in the forest and upper villages. The locals used to raise eight to ten goats and two to four pigs for their livelihood. But the floods have damaged their farms and livestock farming businesses, and they have lost their source of income, he said. According to Tamang, local farmers are facing problems with roads and drinking water after the floods. The floods have destroyed roads and buried drinking water sources and irrigation structures, leading to water shortages. Before the flood, locals were earning a living by cultivating vegetables and other crops in their fields. But now, after the flood washed away the cultivable land and produce, there is no immediate way to earn an income, he said. He said that although the local government has prioritized the work of improving roads and facilitating movement, it is necessary to create an immediate income-generating environment for the affected families. He said, "It would be good if we could create an environment where people living in the upper villages can earn a living again. It has been 10-15 days since we started the work. There is still 10-15 days of search and management work to be done." According to him, the work of searching for and managing animal remains in the flood-affected areas is still ongoing. Similarly, Krish Bahadur Tamang said that work is ongoing to search for animal remains in areas damaged by the floods of Bhadra 20. According to him, searches and investigations have been carried out in most of the flood-affected areas. While animal bones and remains have been found in some places, nothing has been found in others. He said that efforts are being made to identify and manage the remains in the places where they are found. According to Tamang, before the flood, pig and poultry farms were operating in the area. There were shops and livestock farms in the area, where the team working on the hydroelectric project also lived. He estimated that there were two to four pig and chicken farms in the area. He said that efforts are underway to find the remains of the missing animals after the floods caused extensive damage to those farms. Stating that bones were found in some places during the search and not in others, he said that efforts will continue until the search of the entire area is completed. He informed that other materials or remains other than bones have not been found so far.

तामाङका अनुसार बाढीपछि स्थानीय कृषकले सडक र खानेपानीको समस्या भोगिरहेका छन् । बाढीले बाटो भत्काउनुका साथै खानेपानीका मुहान तथा सिँचाइका संरचना पुरिएका कारण पानीको अभावसमेत भएको छ ।

बाढी आउनुअघि स्थानीयले खेतबारीमा तरकारीलगायत खेती गर्दै जीविकोपार्जन गरिरहेका थिए । तर बाढीले खेतीयोग्य जमिन र उत्पादन बगाएपछि अहिले तत्काल आम्दानी गर्ने माध्यम नरहेको उनले बताए ।

स्थानीय सरकारले सडक तथा आवतजावत सहज बनाउने कामलाई प्राथमिकता दिए पनि प्रभावित परिवारका लागि तत्काल आयआर्जनको वातावरण बनाउन आवश्यक रहेको उनको भनाइ छ ।

उनले भने, ‘माथिल्लो गाउँमा बसिरहेका मानिसहरूका लागि फेरि कमाएर खाने वातावरण बनाउन सकियो भने राम्रो हुन्थ्यो। हामीले काम सुरु गरेको १०–१५ दिन भइसक्यो। अझै १०–१५ दिनसम्म खोजी तथा व्यवस्थापनको काम गर्नुपर्ने अवस्था छ ।’

उनका अनुसार बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रमा पशुका अवशेष खोज्ने र व्यवस्थापन गर्ने काम अझै जारी छ ।

यसैगरी, कृषबहादुर तामाङले भदौ १० गतेको बाढीले क्षति पु¥याएका क्षेत्रमा पशुका अवशेष खोज्ने काम जारी रहेको बताए ।

उनका अनुसार बाढी प्रभावित क्षेत्रका अधिकांश स्थानमा खोजी तथा छानबिन गरिएको छ । केही ठाउँमा पशुका हड्डी तथा अवशेष भेटिए पनि कतिपय स्थानमा भने अहिलेसम्म केही फेला परेको छैन । भेटिएका स्थानमा अवशेष पहिचान गर्ने र व्यवस्थापन गर्ने प्रयास भइरहेको उनले बताए ।

तामाङका अनुसार बाढी आउनुअघि उक्त क्षेत्रमा बंगुर तथा कुखुरापालनका फार्महरू सञ्चालनमा थिए । जलविद्युत् आयोजनामा काम गर्ने टोलीसमेत बस्ने गरेको उक्त क्षेत्रमा पसल तथा पशुपालन फार्महरू रहेका थिए ।

उनले आफ्नो अनुमानमा उक्त क्षेत्रमा दुईदेखि चार वटासम्म बंगुर तथा कुखुराका फार्म रहेको बताए। बाढीले ती फार्महरूमा ठूलो क्षति पु¥याएपछि अहिले हराएका पशुका अवशेष खोज्ने काम भइरहेको उनको भनाइ छ ।

खोजीका क्रममा कुनै स्थानमा हड्डी भेटिएको र कुनै स्थानमा नभेटिएको भन्दै उनले सम्पूर्ण क्षेत्रको खोजी पूरा नभएसम्म प्रयास जारी राख्ने बताए। हड्डीबाहेक अन्य सामग्री वा अवशेष भने अहिलेसम्म फेला नपरेको उनले जानकारी दिए ।

Kathmandu. Locals are continuing to search for and manage the remains of animals in the area damaged by the Bhotekoshi flood on Bhadra 10. Locals have become active in searching for the remains of missing animals after the flood damaged pig, goat and poultry farms. Local Phul Bahadur Tamang said that work is underway to search for and manage animal remains in the area damaged by the flood that occurred on Bhadra 20. He said that a committee of 30 people from the ward has been formed to search and clean up the flood-affected area. He informed that work is underway to search for animal bones and remains in flood-damaged pig and goat farms and dig pits to bury the remains found. He said that so far, animal bones have been found in two places and all of them have been managed. He said that the floods have caused major damage to goat and pig farms run by locals in the forest and upper villages. The locals used to raise eight to ten goats and two to four pigs for their livelihood. But the floods have damaged their farms and livestock farming businesses, and they have lost their source of income, he said. According to Tamang, local farmers are facing problems with roads and drinking water after the floods. The floods have destroyed roads and buried drinking water sources and irrigation structures, leading to water shortages. Before the flood, locals were earning a living by cultivating vegetables and other crops in their fields. But now, after the flood washed away the cultivable land and produce, there is no immediate way to earn an income, he said. He said that although the local government has prioritized the work of improving roads and facilitating movement, it is necessary to create an immediate income-generating environment for the affected families. He said, "It would be good if we could create an environment where people living in the upper villages can earn a living again. It has been 10-15 days since we started the work. There is still 10-15 days of search and management work to be done." According to him, the work of searching for and managing animal remains in the flood-affected areas is still ongoing. Similarly, Krish Bahadur Tamang said that work is ongoing to search for animal remains in areas damaged by the floods of Bhadra 20. According to him, searches and investigations have been carried out in most of the flood-affected areas. While animal bones and remains have been found in some places, nothing has been found in others. He said that efforts are being made to identify and manage the remains in the places where they are found. According to Tamang, before the flood, pig and poultry farms were operating in the area. There were shops and livestock farms in the area, where the team working on the hydroelectric project also lived. He estimated that there were two to four pig and chicken farms in the area. He said that efforts are underway to find the remains of the missing animals after the floods caused extensive damage to those farms. Stating that bones were found in some places during the search and not in others, he said that efforts will continue until the search of the entire area is completed. He informed that other materials or remains other than bones have not been found so far.
